source: General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — Sweet Corn Production Handbook (ផលិតកម្មដំណំពោតផ្អែម), in partnership with SNV
text:
Stage 4 — Flowering (ដំណាក់កាលចេញផ្កា): this is the first stage of the Reproductive Formation phase (the 4th overall growth stage), when the male tassel and female silk emerge and pollination occurs, forming the kernels. After pollination, the female flower (silk) is observed growing rapidly, becoming longer and thicker. Corn generally flowers at 40-55 days after planting, depending on the variety. Common problems at this stage include rats, armyworms, corn borers, leaf blight disease, dwarf/yellowing disease, and stiff-leaf disease.

Stage 5 — First grain set (ដំណាក់កាលកកើតគ្រាប់ដំបូង): kernel/ear development begins after the male and female flowers have finished pollinating, when the plant is 47-65 days old after planting. At this stage, both the silk and the ear are observed increasing in length and size. During this period, the endosperm begins to accumulate starch, protein, oil, etc. Problems occurring at this stage are similar to the previous stage, but with the addition of ear-boring worms (corn earworm).

Stage 6 — Milk stage (ដំណាក់កាលដាក់ទឹកដោះ): the stage from ear/tassel swelling until the milk stage, during which the ear continues to grow in both length and width. At this point corn can be harvested young for eating, and each kernel is plump from base to tip and rounded. Each kernel is filled with a milky liquid mixed with starch and other nutrients. During this stage kernels are arranged in rows and beginning to change color; young-ear harvest can occur toward the end of this stage or the beginning of the next. By the end of this stage the plant is 67-85 days old after planting. Problems occurring are similar to prior stages.

Stage 7 — Dough stage (ដំណាក់កាលដាក់ម្សៅ): the stage after the milk has fully converted to dough (soft solid). During this stage, kernels from row to row and ear to ear become tightly packed with a pale yellowish color. This is also when young ears can be harvested, since the kernels are plump base to tip and rounded. At the center of the cob, moisture content drops to 40-50%. The husk becomes shiny, and the outer husk leaves turn from green to a duller color and become slightly drier (husk drying stage). Leaves and stalks change from fresh green to pale green, with leaves beginning to dry out. This stage lasts about 10-15 days, with total age after planting reaching about 77-100 days. Problems occurring are similar to prior stages.

Stage 8 — Maturity (ពេលពោតទុំ): the stage when kernels have fully hardened dough and the ear husk has turned a dull color, until full ripeness. At this stage the plant turns yellow, leaves wilt/droop, kernels harden, husks are shiny and dry, with grain moisture at only about 20-25%. This stage lasts 30-45 days, and total age from planting to maturity is 90-120 days, depending on variety and growing conditions.
